mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A accepts the impossible as an operating fact and immediately arranges its practical consequences.
mechanismDistinction.closestConfusableConcept: Skeptical realism or arbitrary bureaucracy
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: The unusual premise must remain true; the practical response must use one of its actual properties.

alternativeComparison: The meeting organizer schedules recorded prophecy so an audience will still hear it; the prospective housemate bargains over the timing of a gold payment funded by dragon heat. Public-event scheduling and domestic reciprocal payment create different relationships and practical pressures.
situationChange: Keeps the talking ceiling and meeting; a midnight recording and forecast about the finance report replace microphone disbelief and parking cost.
reviewer: Assistant internal two-pass reading; not independent human or live approval.

cards.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay in the flat. Which meter measures its heating?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It breathes fire.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it pays the gas bill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It insists on being called Your Majesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put that on the standing order.

cardFidelity.evidence: A accepts the dragon and its royal title, but paying for gas does not clearly follow from producing fire.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fire prompts a gas charge with no established consumption; the title is directly incorporated into the standing order.

relationship.evidence: B supplies traits rather than negotiating a workable housing arrangement.

heightening.evidence: A5 treats royal dignity as payment paperwork, a useful contrast grounded in the title.

specificity.evidence: Flat, heat, bill and payment are concrete domestic matters.

brevityWit.evidence: Standing order is economical; the causal uncertainty in the gas bill blunts practical realism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay in the flat. Does its fire heat the water?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. You won't need the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Great. It can have the money we save on gas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only accepts payment in gold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could it accept an annual payment? I don't think a month's gas makes a whole coin.

cardFidelity.evidence: A accepts dragon heat and gold payment without surprise and negotiates a budget and payment interval.

responseLogic.evidence: Replacing the boiler supplies the gas savings; gold-only payment prompts pooling those savings over a year.

relationship.evidence: B explains the dragon’s useful contribution and payment constraint, enabling actual household bargaining.

heightening.evidence: A treats a fantasy demand as an issue of cash-flow timing instead of rejecting the housemate.

specificity.evidence: Flat, water heating, boiler savings and a coin give practical substance to the unusual premise.

brevityWit.evidence: The annual-payment request is quietly matter-of-fact; the explanation is useful but less sharp than the strongest endings.

cards.title: The Important Thing
cards.instruction: Choose one ordinary object, phrase, or rule and treat it as vitally important. Keep bringing the scene back to it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody moves out until I find the paperclip from my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The removal van is charging by the hour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the driver help look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He can have the building. I want the paperclip.

cardFidelity.evidence: The paperclip remains more important than a paid van or vacating the building.

responseLogic.evidence: Hourly charges recruit the driver into searching; the keys demand triggers A’s willingness to surrender the building but not the clip.

relationship.evidence: B wants the move completed and adds both financial and possession pressure.

heightening.evidence: A5 explicitly ranks a whole building below the small missing object under a handover deadline.

specificity.evidence: Moving out, desk, van and landlord create a playable situation.

brevityWit.evidence: He can have the building is figurative, since the landlord already owns it; the intended contrast is still legible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You changed 'regards' to 'best regards' in my email.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also got us the contract.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can discuss that after removing 'best.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's worth a million pounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they should respect my regards as they were.

responseLogic.evidence: B2’s contract is postponed for the word correction; B4’s price only prompts renewed insistence on the same wording.

relationship.evidence: B supplies progressively larger inducements but no altered means of handling the email.

heightening.evidence: A5 restates the priority with financial emphasis rather than discovering a new tactic.

specificity.evidence: Email editing and a contract give a natural working relationship.

brevityWit.evidence: Respect my regards is concise but summarizes the fixation rather than developing it.

specificity.evidence: Email, contract and correction supply a credible editing exchange.

brevityWit.evidence: Withdrawn my regards uses B’s remedy to make the innocuous sign-off feel consequential.

cards.title: The Grand Design
cards.instruction: Treat coincidences and interruptions as parts of a larger plan. Connect everything with absolute conviction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two red buses and now your red scarf. We're being directed somewhere.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wear this every day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they've been preparing you for years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone's ringing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Answer it. The timetable's getting impatient.

cardFidelity.evidence: A interprets red coincidences as direction and long preparation, but the plan remains unspecified.

responseLogic.evidence: Daily scarf use extends the supposed timeline; the phone ring becomes an impatient timetable without a link to the red signs.

relationship.evidence: B gives routine facts but has no concrete role beyond being recruited as evidence.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds another portent without clarifying a larger inferred purpose.

specificity.evidence: Buses, scarf and phone are concrete, though their situation or destination is thin.

brevityWit.evidence: Impatient timetable is an abstract button where a causal connection is needed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two red buses and now your red scarf. We're meant to paint the front door red.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You gave me this scarf at Christmas.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've been part of it for months without knowing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbour's asking to borrow our paintbrush.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's been sent to do the painting. Tell him the door will be ready.

cardFidelity.evidence: A gives repeated red objects a purpose, infers past unwitting participation and casts a tool request as recruitment of a worker.

responseLogic.evidence: Being the scarf’s giver places A in the supposed preparation months earlier; the brush request identifies the alleged appointed painter.

relationship.evidence: B corrects who supplied the scarf and brings a neighbor’s practical request that now needs an answer.

heightening.evidence: The plan expands from signs about a door color into past preparation and allocation of the work.

specificity.evidence: Buses, scarf, front door and borrowed brush locate an ordinary neighborhood conversation.

brevityWit.evidence: He has been sent is a sincere inference from borrowing the relevant tool, though the color-to-door leap remains deliberately irrational.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift stopped on three. There are three of us. This is arranged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are four of us.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Message received. We stay together.

cardFidelity.evidence: A converts the lift’s numbers into a messenger theory but never establishes what the arrangement is for.

responseLogic.evidence: Four people causes an invented messenger exception; stopping on four supposedly gives a message without explaining its content.

relationship.evidence: B corrects a count and reports a floor, functioning mainly as a number feeder.

heightening.evidence: Stay together gestures at an instruction but could follow almost any new number.

specificity.evidence: Lift, floor and occupants are clear and require no separate action.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three of us, and the lift stops at three. Someone on this floor needs our help.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are four of us. You missed the courier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's the guide. Ask him which door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's going to five. He's delivering a replacement kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three was where we met our guide. We're going to five; someone needs company for tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A infers a helping mission, recasts the missed courier as a guide and makes the first stop an arranged rendezvous for a visit.

responseLogic.evidence: The fourth person gets a special role; delivery to five redirects the party and the kettle suggests company for tea.

relationship.evidence: B supplies a correction and the courier’s real destination and purpose; A has to absorb all of them into the design.

heightening.evidence: A5 explains why they met at three while assigning everyone a social purpose on five, beyond merely matching a number.

specificity.evidence: The lift, courier, floors and replacement kettle provide a clear chain of events in speech.

brevityWit.evidence: The delivery becomes a mission of companionship. It is gentler and more elaborate than a short punchline.

cards.title: Default Decision-Maker
cards.instruction: Take charge of every small practical choice, treating speed and efficiency as proof that you should remain in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered everyone's sandwiches. We saved six minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm vegetarian.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've already removed your ham. Seven minutes saved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I choose next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could, but I've ordered next time too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A claims saved minutes justify ordering for everyone and pre-empts even the next meal choice.

responseLogic.evidence: Vegetarian preference triggers unilateral ham removal; B’s next-time request exposes that next time is already controlled.

relationship.evidence: B has a dietary preference and asks for future agency, narrowing what A can plausibly call helpful.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends A’s head start into a second occasion specifically raised by B.

specificity.evidence: Sandwich ordering and the removed filling make the work-lunch situation obvious.

brevityWit.evidence: Ordered next time too is caused by B’s exact request, while the minute-count exposes A’s self-serving efficiency measure.

brevityWit.evidence: The next-time reversal is economical and requires B’s proposed future choice.

cards.title: Temporary Authority
cards.instruction: Project brisk confidence through the routine, as though any hesitation would reveal that your authority is only temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm covering reception until two. Deliveries now use the side door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've always used the front.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And we must be decisive during this transition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The receptionist will be back in five minutes.

cards.instruction: Act as the reliable second-in-command, managing access and details while quietly shaping every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The captain's busy. I'll decide which messages reach her.

beats.text: This one changes our route.

cards.instruction: Use another person’s judgment constantly while minimizing how much influence that dependence gives them.
